1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	-/
     5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRankOneOpen
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneNativePresentation
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Assembly from a rank-one divisor-fibre pullback
    10	
    11	This file isolates the last presheaf step in the arbitrary-scheme rank-one fibre construction.
    12	Its input ties an open `W` to the displayed family, supplies native presentations on every
    13	affine pullback, and supplies the canonical evaluation-divisor classifier.  The geometric input
    14	to the assembly theorem is the genuine pullback square of that evaluation divisor along Abel.
    15	The universal property of this stronger square produces, rather than assumes, the factorisation
    16	field of `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`.
    17	
    18	The global construction of the canonical classifier and its represented pullbacks remains an
    19	upstream obligation.  The endpoint here keeps that obligation in its geometric `IsPullback`
    20	form and feeds the resulting arbitrary-scheme fibres immediately to
    21	`picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented`.
    22	
    23	Thus this module is a conditional assembly interface, not the missing global producer: no
    24	declaration below constructs the evaluator, the open family, or its pullback theorem.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	set_option autoImplicit false
    28	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    29	
    30	universe u
    31	
    32	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    33	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    34	
    35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    36	
    37	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    38	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    39	
    40	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    41	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    42	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    43	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    44	
    45	noncomputable section
    46	
    47	abbrev rankOneAmbient : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
    48	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
    49	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))
    50	
    51	abbrev rankOneLocus : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
    52	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
    53	
    54	/-- The divisor families whose Abel class has a rank-one presentation, extended to the big site. -/
    55	abbrev rankOneDivisorLocus : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
    56	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
    57	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor
    58	
    59	/-- The restricted represented Abel map on the big site. -/
    60	def rankOneAbelSigma :
    61	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ⟶
    62	      rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) :=
    63	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (rankOneAbelRepresented pi)
    64	
    65	/-- The ambient class of a divisor already known to lie in the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    66	def rankOneDivisorToAmbient :
    67	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C) :=
    68	  rankOneAbelSigma pi ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi
    69	
    70	/-! ## The explicit geometric input -/
    71	
    72	/-- The single canonical evaluation-divisor classifier used by every represented fibre.
    73	
    74	Keeping this datum outside `PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput` prevents the classifier from
    75	varying with the test scheme or displayed family. -/
    76	structure PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData where
    77	  divisor : rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ⟶
    78	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi)
    79	  divisor_abel : divisor ≫ rankOneAbelSigma pi = 𝟙 _
    80	
    81	namespace PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData
    82	
    83	/-- Applying restricted Abel to the canonical evaluation divisor recovers its rank-one class. -/
    84	lemma divisor_abel_app (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi)
    85	    (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : (rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi)).obj (op S)) :
    86	    (rankOneAbelSigma pi).app (op S) (E.divisor.app (op S) v) = v := by
    87	  exact congrArg (fun q => q.app (op S) v) E.divisor_abel
    88	
    89	/-- The canonical divisor has the original ambient Picard class. -/
    90	lemma divisor_toAmbient (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi) :
    91	    E.divisor ≫ rankOneDivisorToAmbient pi = picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi := by
    92	  rw [rankOneDivisorToAmbient, ← Category.assoc, E.divisor_abel, Category.id_comp]
    93	
    94	/-- The separate uniqueness obligation saying every divisor in the rank-one presentation
    95	preimage is the canonical evaluation divisor of its Abel class. -/
    96	def AbelInverse (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi) : Prop :=
    97	  rankOneAbelSigma pi ≫ E.divisor = 𝟙 _
    98	
    99	/-- Once divisor uniqueness is proved, restricted Abel and canonical evaluation form the
   100	rank-one family isomorphism. -/
   101	def evaluationIso (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi) (h : E.AbelInverse) :
   102	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ≅ rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) where
   103	  hom := rankOneAbelSigma pi
   104	  inv := E.divisor
   105	  hom_inv_id := h
   106	  inv_hom_id := E.divisor_abel
   107	
   108	end PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData
   109	
   110	/--
   111	The explicit data needed to assemble one arbitrary-scheme rank-one fibre.
   112	
   113	`restrictedValue` is the restriction of the displayed ambient family to `W`, and
   114	`nativePresentation` quantifies over every affine pullback of that value.  The parameter `E` is
   115	the common evaluation-divisor classifier on the rank-one locus, with its Abel compatibility
   116	kept explicit.  Divisor representability is deliberately not a field of this structure: it is
   117	supplied separately as a pullback square to the assembly theorem.
   118	
   119	In particular, no field-fibre dimension witness, unrelated line bundle, or pre-existing
   120	`PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented` is accepted by this contract.  Conversely, this structure is not
   121	itself a producer: an inhabitant must still supply the arbitrary-affine native presentations.
   122	-/
   123	structure PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput
   124	    (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi)
   125	    {X : Scheme.{u}}
   126	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C)) where
   127	  W : X.Opens
   128	  restrictedValue : rankOneAmbient (C := C).obj (op (W : Scheme.{u}))
   129	  restrictedValue_eq :
   130	    restrictedValue =
   131	      (yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) (𝟙 (W : Scheme.{u}))
   132	  /-- The tied native presentation on every affine pullback of the restricted family value. -/
   133	  nativePresentation :
   134	    ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   135	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ Over.mk restrictedValue.1),
   136	      Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
   137	        ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op restrictedValue.2))
   138	
   139	namespace PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput
   140	
   141	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
   142	variable {g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C)}
   143	variable {E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi}
   144	
   145	/-- The public-locus element carried by the restricted family value over `W`. -/
   146	noncomputable def locusValue (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g) :
   147	    (rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi)).obj (op (F.W : Scheme.{u})) :=
   148	  ⟨F.restrictedValue.1, ⟨F.restrictedValue.2,
   149	    mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations pi
   150	      (fun A _ _ t => F.nativePresentation A t)⟩⟩
   151	
   152	/-- The map into the public locus is obtained from its universal element by Yoneda. -/
   153	noncomputable def fst (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g) :
   154	    yoneda.obj (F.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) :=
   155	  yonedaEquiv.symm F.locusValue
   156	
   157	/-- The canonical evaluation divisor of the restricted family value over `W`. -/
   158	noncomputable def evaluationDivisor
   159	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g) :
   160	    yoneda.obj (F.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) :=
   161	  F.fst ≫ E.divisor
   162	
   163	/-- The factorisation clause required by `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`, exposed as the target
   164	of the represented evaluation-divisor argument below. -/
   165	def FibreFactorizationClause
   166	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g) : Prop :=
   167	  ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : (rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi)).obj (op S)) (w : S ⟶ X),
   168	    (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) v =
   169	      g.app (op S) w →
   170	    ∃ u : S ⟶ (F.W : Scheme.{u}),
   171	      F.fst.app (op S) u = v ∧ u ≫ F.W.ι = w
   172	
   173	lemma fst_comp_incl (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g) :
   174	    F.fst ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi = yoneda.map F.W.ι ≫ g := by
   175	  apply yonedaEquiv.injective
   176	  rw [yonedaEquiv_comp, fst, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, yonedaEquiv_apply,
   177	    ← F.restrictedValue_eq]
   178	  dsimp [locusValue, picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl,
   179	    CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat]
   180	  rfl
   181	
   182	/-- The family evaluation divisor has the displayed family as its Abel class. -/
   183	lemma evaluationDivisor_abel
   184	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g) :
   185	    F.evaluationDivisor ≫ rankOneDivisorToAmbient pi =
   186	      yoneda.map F.W.ι ≫ g := by
   187	  rw [evaluationDivisor, Category.assoc, E.divisor_toAmbient]
   188	  exact F.fst_comp_incl
   189	
   190	/-! ## The represented rank-one-divisor fibre square -/
   191	
   192	/-- The open `W` represents the pullback of the restricted divisor-class map along the displayed
   193	family, with its top map fixed by the canonical evaluation divisor.  This is stronger than the
   194	factorisation clause for the public rank-one locus: it is a categorical pullback against the
   195	entire restricted rank-one divisor presheaf. -/
   196	def EvaluationDivisorPullback
   197	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g) : Prop :=
   198	  IsPullback
   199	    F.evaluationDivisor
   200	    (yoneda.map F.W.ι)
   201	    (rankOneDivisorToAmbient pi)
   202	    g
   203	
   204	/-- The represented evaluation-divisor square produces the public-locus factorisation on every
   205	test scheme. -/
   206	lemma fibreFactorizationClause_of_evaluationDivisorPullback
   207	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g)
   208	    (hpb : F.EvaluationDivisorPullback) :
   209	    F.FibreFactorizationClause := by
   210	  intro S v w hvw
   211	  have hS := (IsPullback.iff_app.mp hpb) (op S)
   212	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff] at hS
   213	  have hcompat :
   214	      (rankOneDivisorToAmbient pi).app (op S)
   215	          (E.divisor.app (op S) v) =
   216	        g.app (op S) w := by
   217	    have h := congrArg
   218	      (fun q => q.app (op S) v) E.divisor_toAmbient
   219	    change
   220	      (rankOneDivisorToAmbient pi).app (op S)
   221	          (E.divisor.app (op S) v) =
   222	        (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op S) v at h
   223	    rw [h]
   224	    exact hvw
   225	  obtain ⟨u, huDivisor, huW⟩ :=
   226	    hS.2.2 (E.divisor.app (op S) v) w hcompat
   227	  change E.divisor.app (op S) (F.fst.app (op S) u) =
   228	    E.divisor.app (op S) v at huDivisor
   229	  change u ≫ F.W.ι = w at huW
   230	  refine ⟨u, ?_, huW⟩
   231	  calc
   232	    F.fst.app (op S) u =
   233	        (rankOneAbelSigma pi).app (op S)
   234	          (E.divisor.app (op S) (F.fst.app (op S) u)) :=
   235	      (E.divisor_abel_app pi S (F.fst.app (op S) u)).symm
   236	    _ = (rankOneAbelSigma pi).app (op S) (E.divisor.app (op S) v) :=
   237	      congrArg _ huDivisor
   238	    _ = v := E.divisor_abel_app pi S v
   239	
   240	/-! ## Assembly of the stronger fibre datum -/
   241	
   242	/-- Assemble the public fibre presentation from the represented canonical evaluation-divisor
   243	square.  Its `exists_factor` field is derived from the pullback universal property. -/
   244	noncomputable def toFibrePresented_of_evaluationDivisorPullback
   245	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g)
   246	    (hpb : F.EvaluationDivisorPullback) :
   247	    PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g where
   248	  W := F.W
   249	  fst := F.fst
   250	  sq := F.fst_comp_incl
   251	  exists_factor := by
   252	    simpa only [FibreFactorizationClause] using
   253	      F.fibreFactorizationClause_of_evaluationDivisorPullback pi hpb
   254	
   255	@[simp]
   256	lemma toFibrePresented_of_evaluationDivisorPullback_W
   257	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g)
   258	    (hpb : F.EvaluationDivisorPullback) :
   259	    (F.toFibrePresented_of_evaluationDivisorPullback pi hpb).W = F.W :=
   260	  rfl

180	
   181	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   182	-- The residue-field tower and the base-field transition elaborate large curve terms.
   183	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
   184	/-- **The stage degree law at every field point.**  A fibre degree law verified at every
   185	residue field of the stage extends to every field `K` under the stage: the kernel of
   186	`A₀ → K` is a prime `p`, the residue field `κ(p)` embeds in `K` by the universal property
   187	of the residue field (`Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ`), and the degree is invariant under the
   188	base-field transition (`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`). -/
   189	private theorem stage_classDeg_field
   190	    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   191	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R pi)
   192	    (hres : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
   193	      classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   194	        (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass)
   195	        = (genus C : ℤ))
   196	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra R K] [IsScalarTower k R K] :
   197	    classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R K) D.cechPicClass)
   198	      = (genus C : ℤ) := by
   199	  classical
   200	  haveI hker : (RingHom.ker (algebraMap R K)).IsPrime := RingHom.ker_isPrime _
   201	  set p : PrimeSpectrum R := ⟨RingHom.ker (algebraMap R K), hker⟩ with hpdef
   202	  -- the residue field of the kernel prime embeds into `K` over `k`
   203	  have hcompl : p.asIdeal.primeCompl ≤
   204	      (IsUnit.submonoid K).comap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k R K) := by
   205	    intro x hx
   206	    rw [Submonoid.mem_comap]
   207	    exact isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr fun h0 => hx (RingHom.mem_ker.mpr h0)
   208	  let rho : p.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₐ[k] K :=
   209	    Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ p.asIdeal (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k R K) le_rfl hcompl
   210	  letI : Algebra p.asIdeal.ResidueField K := rho.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   211	  haveI : IsScalarTower k p.asIdeal.ResidueField K :=
   212	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (rho.commutes x).symm
   213	  haveI : IsScalarTower R p.asIdeal.ResidueField K :=
   214	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x =>
   215	      (Ideal.ResidueField.liftₐ_algebraMap p.asIdeal
   216	        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k R K) le_rfl hcompl x).symm
   217	  have hcurve : (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap rho).left
   218	      = relCurveMap C p.asIdeal.ResidueField K := by
   219	    refine congrArg
   220	      (fun t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k p.asIdeal.ResidueField =>
   221	        (C ◁ t).left) ?_
   222	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
   223	  have hinv := classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C rho
   224	    (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass)
   225	  rw [hcurve] at hinv
   226	  calc classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R K) D.cechPicClass)
   227	      = classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C p.asIdeal.ResidueField K)
   228	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   229	            D.cechPicClass)) := by
   230	        rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, relCurveMap_comp]
   231	    _ = classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   232	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   233	            D.cechPicClass) := hinv
   234	    _ = (genus C : ℤ) := hres p

   242	/-- **The unique Abel-correct divisor of a rank-one class, Noetherian-free**: over any
   243	affine test whose plus class lies in the rank-one locus there is a unique widened locally
   244	certified divisor class of degree `genus C` whose Abel value is the input class.  No
   245	Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on any carrier; the finite-chart normalization `hpi`
   246	replaces it, feeding the finite-stage descent of the presented datum. -/
   247	theorem existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_mem
   248	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   249	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   250	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
   251	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A))) :
   252	    ∃! F : DivFamZarAff C A (genus C),
   253	      abelDivAffPlus C A F = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1 := by
   254	  classical
   255	  -- membership tested at the identity yields a presentation of the input class
   256	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mp hlam A (𝟙 (overSpec k A))
   257	  have e : ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map
   258	      (𝟙 (overSpec k A)).op lam).1 = lam.1 :=
   259	    picEtMap_id C lam.1
   260	  -- Step 1: descend the presented datum to a finitely generated Noetherian stage with
   261	  -- pair-H¹ vanishing at the stage itself
   262	  have hpair : Subsingleton (datumPair P.datum).H1 :=
   263	    (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing
   264	  obtain ⟨B0, hB0fg, D0, hD0⟩ := P.datum.exists_fg_subalgebra_baseChange_eq
   265	  have hpairBase : Subsingleton
   266	      (datumPair (D0.baseChange (B' := P.cover.Carrier))).H1 := by
   267	    rw [hD0]
   268	    exact hpair
   269	  have htensor : Subsingleton ((datumPair D0).H1 ⊗[B0] P.cover.Carrier) :=
   270	    D0.subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange P.cover.Carrier hpairBase
   271	  obtain ⟨A0, -, -, hAnoeth, hpairA0, hAA⟩ :=
   272	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_fg_pairH1_vanishing_stage
   273	      (C := C) (pi := pi) B0 hB0fg D0 hpi htensor
   274	  letI : IsNoetherianRing A0 := hAnoeth
   275	  letI : Subsingleton (datumPair (D0.baseChange A0)).H1 := hpairA0
   276	  have hbase : (D0.baseChange A0).baseChange P.cover.Carrier = P.datum :=
   277	    hAA.trans hD0
   278	  -- Step 2: fibrewise H¹ witnesses at the stage
   279	  have hfibA : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A0,
   280	      Subsingleton ((datumPair (D0.baseChange A0)).H1 ⊗[A0]
   281	        p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   282	    fun _ => inferInstance
   283	  have hwit : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A0,
   284	      (D0.baseChange A0).HasWitnessH1Vanishing p.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   285	    fun p => ((D0.baseChange A0).hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton
   286	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField).mpr (hfibA p)
   287	  -- stage H⁰ is finite projective over the Noetherian stage
   288	  obtain ⟨-, hfinA, hprojA⟩ := datumRigidEngine (D0.baseChange A0) hpi hfibA
   289	  letI := hfinA
   290	  letI := hprojA
   291	  -- Step 3: the stage rank is one at every prime — the rank-one level set of the locally
   292	  -- constant `rankAtStalk` is clopen and contains the dense image of `Spec B → Spec A₀`
   293	  letI : Module.FinitePresentation A0 (Sheaf.HModule (D0.baseChange A0).sheaf 0) :=
   294	    Module.finitePresentation_of_projective _ _
   295	  have hlc : IsLocallyConstant
   296	      (Module.rankAtStalk (R := A0) (Sheaf.HModule (D0.baseChange A0).sheaf 0)) :=
   297	    Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk
   298	  have hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A0 P.cover.Carrier) :=
   299	    fun x y hxy => Subtype.ext hxy
   300	  have hdense : DenseRange (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A0 P.cover.Carrier)) :=
   301	    PrimeSpectrum.denseRange_comap_iff_ker_le_nilRadical.mpr
   302	      (by rw [(RingHom.injective_iff_ker_eq_bot _).mp hinj]; exact bot_le)
   303	  -- on the image of the comparison the rank is one, transported from the presentation
   304	  set eH0 : P.cover.Carrier ⊗[A0] (Sheaf.HModule (D0.baseChange A0).sheaf 0) ≃ₗ[P.cover.Carrier]
   305	      Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 :=
   306	    ((D0.baseChange A0).datumH0BaseChange P.cover.Carrier hpairA0).trans
   307	      (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv
   308	        (eqToIso (congrArg
   309	          (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C P.cover.Carrier pi => E.sheaf) hbase)) 0)
   310	    with heH0
   311	  have himg : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier,
   312	      Module.rankAtStalk (R := A0) (Sheaf.HModule (D0.baseChange A0).sheaf 0)
   313	        (q.comap (algebraMap A0 P.cover.Carrier)) = 1 := by
   314	    intro q
   315	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange, Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv eH0]
   316	    exact P.h0_rank_one q
   317	  have hrankstage : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A0,
   318	      Module.rankAtStalk (R := A0) (Sheaf.HModule (D0.baseChange A0).sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   319	    intro p
   320	    by_contra hp
   321	    obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hdense.exists_mem_open (hlc ({1}ᶜ : Set ℕ)) ⟨p, hp⟩
   322	    exact hq (himg q)
   323	  -- Step 4: the stage degree law at every field point, by reverse Riemann–Roch
   324	  have hres : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A0,
   325	      classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   326	        (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A0 p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   327	          (D0.baseChange A0).cechPicClass) = (genus C : ℤ) :=
   328	    fun p => stage_classDeg_residueField pi (D0.baseChange A0) hpairA0 p (hrankstage p)
   329	  have hdeg : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra A0 K]
   330	      [IsScalarTower k A0 K],
   331	      classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A0 K)
   332	        (D0.baseChange A0).cechPicClass) = (genus C : ℤ) := by
   333	    intro K _ _ _ _
   334	    exact stage_classDeg_field pi (D0.baseChange A0) hres K
   335	  -- Step 5: the keystone glued divisor at the stage, pushed to the presentation carrier
   336	  obtain ⟨F, hFrel⟩ :=
   337	    (D0.baseChange A0).exists_glued_divFamZarAff_of_admissible_fibre hpi hwit hdeg
   338	  set F' : DivFamZarAff C P.cover.Carrier (genus C) :=
   339	    DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A0 P.cover.Carrier) F with hF'def
   340	  have hF'pic : F'.picClass

    54	/-- **The rank-one divisor uniqueness interface**: over every affine test whose plus class
    55	lies in the rank-one locus, at most one widened locally certified divisor class of degree
    56	`genus C` has Abel value the input class.
    57	
    58	This is the sanctioned missing-item interface of the canonical-divisor route: producers prove

    60	on the rank-one locus is to be discharged by a later session.  Stated as a named `Prop` so
    61	consumers can take it as a single hypothesis. -/
    62	def RankOneDivisorUniqueness : Prop :=
    63	  ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    64	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k S)),
    65	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k S)) →
    66	    ∀ F G : DivFamZarAff C S (genus C),
    67	      abelDivAffPlus C S F = picEtAffineEquiv C S lam.1 →
    68	      abelDivAffPlus C S G = picEtAffineEquiv C S lam.1 → F = G

    70	/-- **Descent of an Abel-correct divisor witness along an étale cover**: a widened divisor
    71	class over the carrier of an étale cover of `A` whose Abel value is the restriction of the
    72	input rank-one plus class descends to a unique Abel-correct widened divisor class over `A`.
    73	
    74	The tensor-square cocycle condition of `DivFamZarAff.exists_descent_of_tensor_eq` is not
    75	assumed: it is manufactured from the uniqueness interface, applied over the tensor square of
    76	the carrier to the two coprojection pullbacks of the witness — both have Abel value the
    77	restriction of the input class along the (single) structure map `A → E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier`,
    78	because the two coprojections agree after the structure map of the cover.  The Abel value of
    79	the descended class is recovered by étale separatedness of `PicEtAff`
    80	(`PicEtAff.map_injective_of_etaleCover`). -/
    81	theorem existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_etale_witness
    82	    (hu : RankOneDivisorUniqueness pi)
    83	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    84	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A))
    85	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A)))
    86	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (F' : DivFamZarAff C E.Carrier (genus C))
    87	    (habel : abelDivAffPlus C E.Carrier F' =
    88	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
    89	        (picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1)) :
    90	    ∃! F : DivFamZarAff C A (genus C),
    91	      abelDivAffPlus C A F = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1 := by
    92	  classical
    93	  set φ0 : A →ₐ[k] E.Carrier := (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k with hφ0
    94	  set φL : E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
    95	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft :
    96	      E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k with hφL
    97	  set φR : E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
    98	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
    99	      E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).restrictScalars k with hφR

   102	  have hψR : φR.comp φ0 = ψ := by
   103	    rw [hψ]
   104	    exact AlgHom.ext fun a =>
   105	      ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
   106	        E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).commutes a).trans
   107	        ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft :
   108	          E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier).commutes a).symm
   109	  -- the input class restricted to the tensor square stays in the rank-one locus
   110	  set lam_sq : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ)
   111	      (overSpec k (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier)) :=
   112	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map (Over.overSpecMap ψ).op lam with hlam_sq_def

   114	      (op (overSpec k (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier))) :=

   126	      = picEtAffineEquiv C (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) lam_sq.1 := by
   127	    rw [hsq, ← abelDivAffPlus_mapAlgHom φR F', habel, ← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, hψR]
   128	  -- uniqueness over the tensor square manufactures the descent cocycle
   129	  have htensor : DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φL F' = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φR F' :=
   130	    hu (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) lam_sq hlam_sq _ _ habelL habelR

   141	    exact hmapF
   142	  exact ⟨F, habelF, fun G hG => hu A lam hlam G F hG habelF⟩

   144	/-- **The unique Abel-correct divisor of a rank-one local presentation**: over a rank-one
   145	plus class with a tied local presentation on a Noetherian étale carrier, there is a unique

   148	Existence: the finite glue

   152	theorem existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation

   154	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]

   161	    P.exists_glued_rankOne_away_divisor_with_abel_evaluation
   162	  exact existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_etale_witness pi hu lam hlam P.cover F0 habel

   164	/-- **The canonical rank-one divisor of a presentation**: the unique widened divisor class
   165	over the test algebra whose Abel value is the presented rank-one plus class, chosen from
   166	`existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation`.  By uniqueness, the choice does not

   169	noncomputable def canonicalRankOneDivisorOfPresentation
   170	    (hu : RankOneDivisorUniqueness pi)
   171	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   172	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
   173	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A)))
   174	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier] :
   175	    DivFamZarAff C A (genus C) :=
   176	  (existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation pi hu hlam P).choose

   178	/-- The canonical rank-one divisor satisfies the Abel equation: its widened Abel value is
   179	the presented rank-one plus class. -/
   180	theorem canonicalRankOneDivisorOfPresentation_abel
   181	    (hu : RankOneDivisorUniqueness pi)
   182	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   183	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
   184	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A)))
   185	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier] :
   186	    abelDivAffPlus C A (canonicalRankOneDivisorOfPresentation pi hu hlam P)
   187	      = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1 :=
   188	  (existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation pi hu hlam P).choose_spec.1

---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling

--- AGENTS ---
This is an **Archon Horizon** workspace: AI agents formalize mathematics in
Lean 4 here, across one or more projects.

Before doing anything else, load the **`horizon`** skill — read
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`. It explains the workspace layout, the
`horizon` CLI, the git/commit conventions, and the session discipline
(one-shot: run work in the foreground and block on it).

---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

    32	/-!
    33	# Narrow root for the AJCR-first Picard strategy
    34	
    35	This root deliberately imports only the current route modules and contracts. Every later
    36	contract endpoint must be checked here before it receives critical-path credit.
    37	
    38	The tied local rank-one presentation, its canonical evaluation map, datum-side local-away
    39	divisor equations, and the pullback-stable presentation locus are present. The conditional
    40	`DivRankOneOpenData` representer and its open-immersion/base-change consumers are rooted. The
    41	native evaluation section and the tied datum section have the same restriction-vanishing
    42	predicate on every open, without a Noetherian hypothesis; their piece coordinates and principal
    43	piece ideals agree, and those native-coordinate ideals commute with arbitrary affine
    44	coefficient extension.
    45	
    46	The native rank-one route now closes from certificates to public membership on the field fibre.
    47	`RankOneFamilyCertificates.ofActualDatum` produces all four family certificates from a single
    48	per-residue-field H1 witness plus a fibre class-degree law, with rank one computed
    49	Noetherian-freely by `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_actualPairH1`. Arbitrary-cartesian
    50	native base change is internalized by `isIso_canonicalBaseChangeMap_nativeModule`, so
    51	`ofCertificatesWithNativeBaseChange` and `ofLocalPresentation` build native presentations with
    52	no extra base-change certificate. Consequently `mem_picRankOneOpen_of_isSplitWitness` places
    53	every split genus-degree field class in `PicRankOneOpen`, and the Pic0 separably closed
    54	translated-cover feeder lands its translated layer element in the public locus:
    55	`exists_sepClosedTranslated_mem_picRankOneOpen` is the phase-5 membership endpoint.
    56	
    57	On the divisor side, the tied local presentation's finite principal-open evaluation divisors
    58	glue: `exists_glued_rankOne_away_divisor_with_abel_evaluation` produces a `DivFamZarAff` over
    59	the Noetherian etale carrier with the global Abel and relative-Picard identities, resting on
    60	`baseOpenRankOneDivisor_awayMul_compat`. The big-site consumer scaffold reduces
    61	`PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen` to one canonical evaluation-divisor classifier and per-test pullback
    62	squares: `picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_evaluationDivisorPullbackFamilies`.
    63	
    64	The glued divisor now descends: `existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation` consumes
    65	the finite-glue output and returns the unique Abel-correct `DivFamZarAff` over the original
    66	affine base, conditional only on the named `RankOneDivisorUniqueness` interface (the
    67	tensor-square cocycle is manufactured from uniqueness, the descended class is pinned by étale
    68	separatedness); `canonicalRankOneDivisorOfPresentation` names that divisor. Toward discharging
    69	the uniqueness interface, `exists_notMem_cechPicMap_eq_of_relPicMk_eq` localizes
    70	`relPicMk`-equality to on-the-nose `picClass` equality near every prime (base Picard classes
    71	die Zariski-locally). The public locus is fibrewise split:
    72	`mem_picRankOneOpen_iff_isSplitWitness` at field bases, and
    73	`isSplitWitness_testPoint_of_mem` at every point of an arbitrary test.
    74	
    75	Fibre nonvanishing toward that discharge is landed:
    76	`sectionsMapTop_ne_zero_of_divEq_certified` and its tensor-form consumer say a datum section
    77	cutting a certified divisor is nonzero on every residue-field fibre — the exact input shape of
    78	the rank-one unit-extraction engine.
    79	
    80	Datum-section extraction is landed, Noetherian-free:
    81	`exists_gluedSection_sectionLocalEquations_divEq` cuts any `LocalEquations` divisor whose
    82	Picard class matches the datum's Čech class from a germ-regular global section of the glued
    83	sheaf, up to `DivEq` on every subordinated pointed cover — the α-corrected gluing through the
    84	glued sheaf's own sheaf property; and `sectionLocalEquations_smul_divEq` records that global
    85	unit rescalings of the section do not move the cut divisor.
    86	
    87	The uniqueness interface is now DISCHARGED: `divFamZarAff_eq_of_picClass_eq_cechPicClass`
    88	proves at most one certified divisor family per rank-one datum class (extraction + fibre
    89	nonvanishing + the unit-extraction engine), and `rankOneDivisorUniqueness` assembles it with
    90	the base-discrepancy localization, away-span separatedness, and faithfully-flat descent into
    91	an unconditional proof of `RankOneDivisorUniqueness`. The canonical rank-one divisor and its
    92	Abel/uniqueness accessors are re-exported without the interface hypothesis
    93	(`canonicalRankOneDivisor`).
    94	
    95	The Abel inverse law is also discharged: `divFamZarAff_eq_of_rankOne` upgrades the affine
    96	uniqueness to arbitrary tests through the vehicle's affine-open separatedness, so the
    97	restricted Abel map is componentwise injective on the big site
    98	(`rankOneAbelSigma_app_injective`) and every evaluation-divisor classifier is automatically a
    99	two-sided inverse (`abelInverse_of_uniqueness`); `rankOneAbelIso` packages the isomorphism,
   100	gated only on an inhabitant of `PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData`.
   101	
   102	Still missing, and NOT replaced here by axioms or local hypotheses: existence of Abel-correct
   103	witnesses over non-Noetherian affine bases (the presentation carrier must currently be
   104	Noetherian), an inhabitant of `PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData` (the canonical global divisor
   105	/ Abel section), `PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen` itself, and the later
   106	representability/descent/`JacobianData` endpoints.
   107	-/

     8	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Image
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    12	
    13	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    14	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    15	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    16	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    17	
    18	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    19	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    20	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    21	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    22	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    27	
    28	universe u
    29	
    30	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    35	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    36	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    37	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    38	
    39	noncomputable section
    40	
    41	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    42	
    43	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    44	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    45	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    46	def PicRankOneOpen :
    47	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    48	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    49	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    50	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    51	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    52	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    53	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    54	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    55	      apply Subtype.ext
    56	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    57	    rw [e]
    58	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    59	
    60	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
    61	
    62	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
    63	
    64	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
    65	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    66	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
    67	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    68	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    69	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
    70	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    71	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    72	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    73	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    74	
    75	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    76	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    77	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    78	contract. -/
    79	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    80	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    81	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    82	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    83	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    84	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    85	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
    86	  rfl
    87	
    88	/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
    89	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    90	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    91	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    92	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    93	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    94	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    95	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    96	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
    97	  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h
    98	
    99	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
   100	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
   101	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   102	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   103	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
   104	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   105	  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h
   106	
   107	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   108	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   109	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   110	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   111	
   112	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   113	
   114	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   115	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   116	relative-open gate below. -/
   117	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   118	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   119	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   120	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   121	
   122	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
   123	
   124	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   125	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
   126	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
   127	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
   128	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)
   129	
   130	/-! ## The explicit fibre producer contract -/
   131	
   132	/-- A fibre of the rank-one locus over one test class, presented by an open of that test.
   133	
   134	The `exists_factor` field is tied to the displayed class `g` and to an arbitrary source value `v`.
   135	It is the family-level content needed for relative representability; the open immersion itself
   136	supplies uniqueness of the factor.  Thus this structure cannot be inhabited by an unrelated open
   137	or by a fieldwise dimension statement. -/
   138	structure PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   139	    {X : Scheme.{u}}
   140	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   141	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))) where
   142	  W : X.Opens
   143	  fst : yoneda.obj (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   144	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
   145	  sq : fst ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
   146	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u})
   147	    (v : (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor).obj (Opposite.op S))
   148	    (w : S ⟶ X),
   149	    (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (Opposite.op S) v =
   150	      g.app (Opposite.op S) w →
   151	    ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}),
   152	      fst.app (Opposite.op S) u = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
   153	
   154	namespace PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   155	
   156	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
   157	variable {g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   158	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))}
   159	
   160	/-- The fibre square supplied by `FibrePresented` is a pullback of presheaves. -/
   161	theorem isPullback (D : PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   162	    IsPullback D.fst (yoneda.map D.W.ι) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g := by
   163	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
   164	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
   165	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   166	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   167	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) =>
   168	      φ.app S) D.sq
   169	  · rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
   170	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp h₂
   171	  · intro v w hvw
   172	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
   173	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
   174	
   175	end PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   176	
   177	/-- An arbitrary-test fibre producer discharges the relative openness gate. -/
   178	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented
   179	    (D : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
   180	      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   181	        Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))),
   182	      PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   183	    PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi := by
   184	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists ?_
   185	  intro X g
   186	  let d := D X g
   187	  exact ⟨d.W, d.fst, d.W.ι, d.isPullback, inferInstance⟩
   188	
   189	/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
   190	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
   191	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
   192	  h
   193	
   194	/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
   195	pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
   196	theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
   197	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   198	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   199	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   200	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
   201	    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
   202	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
   203	    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
   204	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
   205	    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   206	  h.property g fst snd hpb
   207	
   208	/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
   209	theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   210	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   211	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   212	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   213	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h
   214	
   215	/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/
   216	theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   217	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   218	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   219	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   220	  picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi f h
   221	
   222	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
   223	
   224	This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
   225	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
   226	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
   227	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
   228	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   229	
   230	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
   231	representer. -/
   232	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
   233	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
   234	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
   235	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   236	
   237	/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   238	def rankOneAbelAff :
   239	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
   240	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   241	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   242	
   243	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   244	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
   245	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   246	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
   247	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
   248	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   249	
   250	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   251	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
   252	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   253	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
